claim: Production v3 catalyst+sentiment additions deliver +7.46% mean 7d return
what_was_wrong: +14.6pp lift in 2024 vs -0.3pp in 2025 — unstable across years. Mean was misleading; median tells truth.
correction: Always report median alongside mean; flag instability when years diverge >2x
lesson: Mean returns are fat-tail-corrupted. If 2024 and 2025 diverge by 14pp, the strategy isn't generalising.

claim: Joint signal stacking — 3+ confirmations → 80%+ confidence
what_was_wrong: Empirically falsified by joint_signal_analyzer.py: 3-signal stocks have 40.4% hit rate vs 42.8% baseline. Signals correlate, don't multiply.
correction: Removed stacking thesis; signals identified as non-independent in code

claim: Multibagger basket: 26 names at 0.86+ → 90% calibrated to double in 180d
what_was_wrong: Calibration was in-sample. User-corrected risk_envelope.py: real prospective hit rate is 12.4% per name (41% basket-level), NOT 90%. Expected ann is -1% (negative EV) without regime gate.
correction: find_180d_frontier_honest.py uses strict prospective protocol (calibrate on 2024 only, test on 2025 only). Real number: max uptick at 80% confidence = 15% in 180d.
lesson: Isotonic on the same OOF being scored is leakage. Must fit calibrator on strictly prior data.

claim: Strategy delivers 30-50% ann (and 262% expected per multibagger basket)
what_was_wrong: 9-year backtest forced top-5 trades EVERY day, including chop days when no name had 0.95+ score → 2018, 2019 negative because of this. With dynamic gate (cash on no-fire days), 9-year median is +8% ann (cash-dominated)
correction: backtest_dynamic_gated.py implements the right test. Honest 9-year median: ~+8% with worst year +7% (cash). Below 30% min target.
lesson: Dynamic > static. The discipline gate transforms outcome distribution. To hit 30%+ unlevered, need market-neutral overlay or wider gate.

claim: Agent prompts in prompts/ directory are routed through every user request
what_was_wrong: Prompts existed as documentation only; not programmatically invoked. Devil's advocate fired AFTER claims, not before.
correction: Built run_agent.py to programmatically invoke any prompt as a Claude API system message. Going forward, material claims must run through devils_advocate first.
lesson: Documented standards are not enforced standards. Must be runtime-wired.

claim: find_high_conviction.py auto-loads scr_*, qvm_*, acad_* prefix features and produces calibrated daily picks
what_was_wrong: 47 of those features (18 Screener + 20+ QVM + 9 Academic) are point-in-time today-snapshots broadcast as constant per-symbol values across all historical training rows. The 2018 training rows for RELIANCE get the same scr_pe (today's), qvm_qvm_rank (today's), and acad_mom_12_1 (computed from 2026 closing prices) as the 2026 rows. Severity: CATASTROPHIC look-ahead. Every claim emitted by find_high_conviction.py since the extras were enabled is structurally inflated. Developer comment in build_academic_alphas.py L194-L195 acknowledges the design: 'academic_alphas only has TODAYS snapshot. We broadcast it forward as a static feature (same caveat as Screener fundamentals).'
correction: 1) All find_high_conviction outputs marked CONTAMINATED in HANDOFF until time-series fundamentals layer ships. 2) Detailed audit at reports/leakage_audit_20260501.md. 3) Remediation: build proper effective_from_date join from data/fundamentals_full_history/ archives; rebuild derived_ratios + academic_alphas with per-date semantics; drop snapshot-broadcast columns until rebuilt.
lesson: Auto-discovery of features by prefix is a leak amplifier. Any feature whose value is constant per symbol across all dates is either a leak or useless. Build a contract: every feature must vary per (symbol, date) OR be explicitly justified as constant.

claim: backtest_dynamic_gated.py and find_180d_frontier_honest.py results are honest
what_was_wrong: Audit verified these two scripts ingest only BASE_FEATS (price/technical) and do NOT touch the leaked screener/qvm/academic columns. So their published numbers (~85% prospective hit @ +15%/180d, +8% 9-year median ann) survive the leakage audit.
correction: No correction needed; honest claims preserved. But note: any future ensemble or stacked variant must declare which feature columns it ingests and prove they pass the (symbol, date) variance check.
lesson: Compartmentalization saved us. The two pipelines that DID stay close to the discipline of HANDOFF turned out to be the only publishable ones. Future model variants should default to BASE_FEATS-only until extra features are independently validated.

claim: stock_daily_facts_adjusted_2015plus.parquet is split/bonus adjusted as the filename suggests
what_was_wrong: Audit triggered by user question 'split etc taken into account hai na?' Found a real adjustment hole. Sample failures: BESTAGRO 1:2 bonus on 2026-01-16 went UNADJUSTED in the price series — close 289.47 → 29.65 (a phantom -89.8% drop) on the ex-date. Multiple gold/silver ETFs (HDFCMFGETF, SETFGOLD, LICMFGOLD, GOLDBEES, etc.) show similar -99% drops on what are clearly unit-restructuring dates. The corporate_actions table itself appears to undercount the actual factor for BESTAGRO (recorded adjustment_factor=1.5 vs observed price dilution ~10x). This means the model's training data contains phantom -90% returns for some symbols, biasing the 9-year base rate of '2x in 180d' UPWARD because some of those 'doubles' were actually bonus-event reversals from a phantom-low close.
correction: 1) Today's live prediction (live_predictions/2026-05-04.json): top-5 picks (KENNAMET, KOVAI, NOVARTIND, AUSOMENT, KIRLFER) audited individually — none have splits/bonuses or suspect price jumps; per-name integrity preserved. The forward outcome measurement is also clean because the broker handles the position-side adjustment automatically. 2) The model's calibrator (8.47% prospective base rate, score_100pct values) has unknown upward bias from contaminated training; absolute probability claims should be treated as strong relative rankings. 3) Remediation: build src/agentic/apply_adjustments.py that uses corporate_actions.parquet to back-adjust the close series symbol-by-symbol with the correct factor, then regenerate stock_daily_facts_adjusted_2015plus.parquet from raw + the new adjustment layer. Also: cross-validate corporate_actions adjustment_factor against the observed price-jump magnitude on each ex_date, flag mismatches. 4) Add CI test: tests/test_no_unadjusted_corporate_actions.py asserts no symbol has a single-day drop sharper than -25% on any date that overlaps a corporate_actions ex_date.
lesson: Filename suffixes lie. _adjusted in a filename is a label, not a contract. Verify by sampling known-event dates (RELIANCE 2017 bonus, INFY 2018 bonus, ADANIPOWER 2025 split) and checking the actual price series. The user's instinct ('split etc taken into account hai na?') was the right rigor question.

claim: Adding ret_60d + off_52w_high features would improve the missed-winner classifier (suggested by 10-session miss attribution: 247/395 winners killed at QC shared strong 60d trend + 52wH proximity)
what_was_wrong: On 3 test windows the new features looked better (p@8 12.5%->16.7%). On the full 13-week walk-forward since April they were WORSE: p@30 -5.4pp, losing 9 of 13 weeks. The 3-window result was noise.
correction: Features rejected; baseline 22-feature model retained. Columns kept in loader for future tests but NOT in FEATURES.
lesson: Never deploy a model change validated on <10 walk-forward windows. The since-April walk-forward (13 weeks) is the minimum bar for classifier changes. Also validated: baseline model p@30 = 39.0% vs 23.0% random (+16pp, positive 12/13 weeks) - the model earns its place; trainer dates were frozen at May/June and now roll dynamically.

claim: Vol-normalized (z-score) entry bands should beat absolute bands — each stock judged on its own scale
what_was_wrong: Nothing — the hypothesis PASSED its pre-registered bar: pool touch rate 55.9% vs 54.1% (10-yr), 60.1% vs 55.7% (since-April); the Z-only cohort (names absolute bands miss) touched 60.1%/68.7% — best bucket in the test. Caveat recorded honestly: top-8-by-delivery C2 realized showed no lift (-0.01% vs -0.02% 10-yr) — the gain is pool-level; downstream ML/ranking must convert it.
correction: apply_qc_filter switched to z-bands (RSI_z [-1,+0.25] vs own 252d dist; ret20d/ret5d in own-vol units). band_fit ranking and all downstream unchanged. Weekly RANK CHECK + scorer are the live judges.
lesson: Granularity as NORMALIZATION (per-stock scale, universal rule) keeps passing tests: vol-scaled stops, now z-bands. Granularity as per-stock rules stays banned (n too small).

claim: Inside the high-vol cohort there is a sub-cohort with the highest positive returns (user hypothesis: AI should find high-vol-GOOD vs high-vol-BAD)
what_was_wrong: The claim SURVIVED row-level discipline (crashedHV+rsi_z<-1: conf-era +2.98%/15d, t=10.1, positive 12/12 years) but FAILED the investable test: top-8/week portfolio of the same cell nets +0.04%/trade, worst week -67%, maxDD -89%. Root cause: crash-cohort rows CLUSTER in capitulation weeks (2025 n=986, 2026 n=618) — row-weighted means are dominated by fat crisis weeks that a fixed 8-name weekly portfolio cannot harvest; row t-stats treated correlated same-week rows as independent. Also confirmed: C2 geometry is destructive on this cohort (-0.21%/trade) — deep-trough recoverers need hold-geometry, proving exit rules must be cohort-conditional.
correction: Nothing ships. Next miner iteration pre-registered: (a) cluster-robust stats (weekly-mean unit, not rows) from the start, (b) market-regime as a declared dimension (is the edge just crisis-week beta?), (c) cohort-specific exit geometry in the same test.
lesson: Row-level t-stats on clustered panels are a trap — the investable unit is the WEEK. The point of the discipline is exactly this: we found the seductive cell AND killed it before it killed capital. Average traders ship the +2.98% row-stat and die in the -89% drawdown.

what: 153 split/bonus (symbol,ex_date) groups had no adjustment_factor because the NSE subject parser required 'Rs' on both sides of a face-value split while NSE writes the target as 'Re 1/-'. 127 symbols carried unadjusted cliffs (fake -50%..-90% returns: TATASTEEL 2022, NESTLEIND 2024, KOTAKBANK 2026-01, DRREDDY 2024, EICHERMOT 2020, TRENT 2016). Additionally: 6 bogus factors (NCRPS/preference bonuses + never-executed splits) had WRONGLY divided history (TVSMOTOR fake +398%, SIYSIL fake +1772% single-row seam), and 11 same-day split+bonus combos were under-adjusted because only one leg carried a factor (BAJFINANCE 2025-06: applied 5, real 10).
root_cause: SPLIT_RATIO_RE regex missed 'Re'; bonus regex parsed non-equity NCRPS bonuses; prices rebuilt before CA store refresh so late-arriving CAs never re-derived rows (same class as 2026-08-18 113-day rot).
blast_radius: 159 symbols / ~163k rows rebuilt. All backtests before 2026-08-28 (C2 tournament, z-band A/B, 10-yr walk-forwards) ran on this corrupted panel — conclusions need re-validation. 2026-08-27 provisional basket verified clean (zero overlap with corrupted set) but was regenerated on repaired data anyway.
fix: src/agentic/repair_ca_adjustments.py: tape-first validation (factor applied only where raw price ratio at ex confirms within 20%, incl. suspension-gap handling: last-pre-trade uncapped), fills/nulls/normalizes store factors, rebuilds affected symbols from raw_* via the production adjuster, recomputes rolling features, verifies zero factor mismatches + close==raw*factor. Two rounds: 157 then 2 symbols. SUMEETINDS (tape 3.06 vs subject 5.0) and KOTYARK (no tape effect for factor 11) left raw and flagged for human review.
prevention: (1) parser accepts Rs/Re and rejects NCRPS/preference/debenture/warrant bonuses; (2) run_weekly_pipeline.sh refreshes CA store BEFORE prices (new src/agentic/refresh_corporate_actions.py step 00); (3) refresh_prices.py LATE-CA SELF-HEAL: every run scans stored price_adjustment_factor_to_present vs the CA store's expected step function and auto-rebuilds mismatched symbols from raw.
verified_by: post-repair scan: 0 factor mismatches across all symbols; max relative residual close vs raw*factor = 0.0; all repaired ex-date windows show |return_1d| < 30%.

what: Pre-registered sleeve walk-forward A/B (10yr, quarterly-retrained hc-replica): UNION (hc top-10 P(+20%/30d) ∪ fresh-IPO ignition) with FIXED 100td hold nets +4.59%/trade (disc<=22) and +9.57%/trade (conf>=23, 75% yrs+). The 'exits are the leverage' intuition from the April window was WRONG under walk-forward.

what: Pre-registered A/B: event-history features (orders_90d, filings, insider/promoter PIT, SHP deltas, days_since_print, results_dump & pre_print_thrust flags) added to a price-only LGBM on the contract target P(+5% touch/15td), identical yearly walk-forward folds 2018-2026. claim: 'Affected price history re-derived and verified' after the 2026-08-27 split-regex fix (SHOWCASE §Honesty 2026-08-18 entry).
what_was_wrong: The regex fix only applied to rows fetched AFTER 08-27; refresh_corporate_actions.py merged new rows and never re-parsed the 26,092 existing ones. 59 historical splits stayed factor-less (JSWSTEEL 2017 -90%, TTL 2025, DBEIL 2026-06-19) and 13 same-day bonus+split pairs carried only the bonus half (CUPID store 2x vs raw 12.6x, SBC 2x vs 29.6x, SUNILHITEC 2x vs 19x). Pre-2018 NSE wording 'Fv Splt Frm Rs 10 To Re 1' matched no pattern at all. Found by the new tests/test_no_unadjusted_corporate_actions.py on its first run: 21 split/bonus ex-dates with < -25% adjusted drops, 80 with any CA.
correction: SPLIT_RATIO_RE accepts 'splt'/'frm'; refresh_corporate_actions.py re-parses the WHOLE store every run (store = f(subject text, current parser), source_note uniform, nothing hand-edited) so a parser improvement heals history; 51 (symbol, ex_date) effective factors change, 23/24 checkable ones move closer to the raw ex-date close ratio (1 NCRPS non-equity case inconclusive). refresh_prices.py LATE-CA SELF-HEAL re-adjusts the affected symbols on the next data-layer run.
lesson: A parser fix is not a data fix. Any store derived from text must be re-derived end-to-end when the parser changes, and a test must assert the OUTPUT (adjusted series), not the code path.

claim: HC engine (find_high_conviction.py) trains on 142 features incl. 123 'engineered' extras, all leak-gated since 2026-05-01.
what_was_wrong: (1) 16 macro_sent__* columns in the SAFE 'macro_' prefix are one headline-sentiment snapshot broadcast to all 1.56M rows (nunique == 1 file-wide) — the 05-01 leak class, slipping through because the CI test only ran the per-symbol median and the coverage gaps of sec_*/wiki_* (null for 2/3 of symbols) made the failure list noisy enough to ignore. (2) data/derived/extra_features.parquet ends 2026-06-17 and is not in the 27-check freshness gate; since then every production HC run has median-filled all 123 extras for the 3 months of rows that matter most (logs/weekly_pipeline/20260908_e_hc.log: 'joined 123 engineered features'). Silent staleness — the exact class the gate was built for.
correction: macro_sent quarantined in LEAKING_EXTRA_PREFIXES and excluded in the loader (constant → zero splits → predictions unchanged). Test now flags any file-wide constant and judges per-symbol variation among covered symbols only. The stale-extras problem is NOT fixed here: wiring feature_factory.py into the weekly data layer + an EXTRA_FEATURES freshness contract needs a memory-profiled run first (5M-row panel; memory law) and a walk-forward A/B of fresh-extras vs median-filled — recorded in logs/debt_ledger.jsonl, owner decision pending.
lesson: Every file an engine reads must sit behind the freshness gate, including 'optional' joins. Median-filling an absent feature is a silent model change, not a no-op.

claim: One canonical store per dataset, gate-protected (2026-08-18 correction, SHOWCASE §Honesty).
what_was_wrong: Announcements still had two stores. refresh_announcements.py (the script the weekly AND daily layers call) wrote only tmp/from_scratch_7d_run/alt/corp_announcements.parquet; the canonical data/events_full_history/normalized/stock_announcements.parquet that the gate, build_news_event_features and tape_forensics read was advanced only by hand-written heredocs inside dated run scripts (monday_run_20260824.sh, friday_run_20260828.sh). Last such run: 2026-08-27. Gate caught it on 2026-09-19 at 16 bd stale — the contract worked, the fix behind it had never been made durable.
correction: refresh_announcements.py now refreshes the canonical store FIRST through the production ingester (dedup sequence_id+symbol, keep last) and raises on an empty fetch; the tmp/ raw store is kept only as catalyst_tagger's input.
lesson: A fix that lives in a dated run script is not a fix. The canonical writer must be the script the schedulers call, and the gate contract must name the file that writer writes.

claim: run_weekly_pipeline.sh step 1 'refreshes all data' before the engines.
what_was_wrong: It ran 6 scripts; build_macro_panel.py only CONSOLIDATES derived files and fetches nothing. The real fetchers (forex, commodities, FRED rates, breadth, India VIX) live in daily_data_layer.sh, last run 2026-09-08. The panel therefore carried a fresh 2026-09-18 trade_date spine over 09-07 breadth, 09-04 dxy, 09-10 us_10y/us_vix, 09-14 usdinr — the exact file-fresh/column-rotten pattern of 2026-07-01. Column-level checks caught 4 of them; breadth_* columns are NOT in the contract and would have gone through silently.
correction: Weekly step 1 now calls daily_data_layer.sh (one data layer). TODO in debt ledger: add breadth_50 / adv_decl_ratio column checks to the MACRO_PANEL contract; 7 FRED spread columns (hy_oas, ig_oas, yc_10y2y, fed_funds, eurusd, usdcny, usdjpy) dead since 2026-04-30/05-07 — either fix fetch_global_rates.py or drop them from the panel.
lesson: 'Refresh' means fetch + consolidate. A consolidator alone can only make stale data look fresh.

claim: run_weekly_pipeline.sh verifies the emitted basket file before proceeding to forensics/reports/commit.
what_was_wrong: It looked for live_predictions/${DATE}_15d5pct.json with DATE fixed at pipeline start, while generate_hybrid_basket.py names the file by date.today() at emit. The 2026-09-19 run slept with the lid closed and emitted 2026-09-21_15d5pct.json; the check declared FAIL on a basket that passed all three convergence checks, and steps 4.3-5 (tape forensics, reports, recreation kit) never ran for it.
correction: BASKET_FILE = newest *_15d5pct.json modified in the last 2h; DATE re-derived from its name. sgm_daily.sh + cron schedule (sgm_schedule.sh) added so the daily layer and daily-actions report run every session without a human launcher.
lesson: Any two places that compute 'today' independently will disagree the first time a run crosses midnight. Derive the date from the artifact, not the clock.

claim: BE/BZ series gap repaired and the fix 'applied identically to the main checkout' (reports/be_series_gap_repair_20260828.md); freshness gate 27/27 green means the price panel is sound.
what_was_wrong: The build_daily_facts.py fix was never committed to any branch; the working copy was overwritten on 2026-09-10 (file mtime) and refresh_prices.py went back to EQ-only. From 2026-09-08 to 09-23 the panel carried 0 BE/BZ rows: ~260-277 traded symbols (9% of the investable universe) missing every session, including TBZ/ALPHAGEO/KALYANIFRG of the live leader sleeve and KRONOX of the paper sleeve. All 27 freshness checks passed throughout — file max-date, column last-non-null and continuity cannot see a missing SYMBOL. The 09-21 and 09-23 baskets were generated on this reduced universe; the leader-sleeve return I quoted used TBZ's 09-22 close as if it were 09-23.
correction: EQUITY_SERIES/T2T_SERIES restored in build_daily_facts.py with T2T delivery imputation; new eval_panel_coverage.py (raw bhavcopy = ground truth: universe coverage >=99.5%, BE/BZ presence, watched-name presence, silent drop-offs, raw-close match) writes logs/evals/ and is the 28th gate contract PANEL_COVERAGE; wired into sgm_daily.sh and the weekly pipeline before the gate; tests/test_panel_coverage.py; repair_coverage_now.sh re-inserts the 12 lost sessions via repair_be_series_gaps.py.
lesson: Freshness is not completeness. A gate that only checks the newest row will pass a panel that lost a tenth of its stocks. And a fix that exists only in a working copy is one checkout away from vanishing — the commit is the fix.

claim: live_predictions/ is an immutable forward record (CONSTITUTION; sgm-orient: NEVER rewrite a committed live_predictions/ file).
what_was_wrong: Nothing in code enforced it. generate_hybrid_basket.py named the file str(date.today()) on the laptop clock (EDT). The off-cadence convergence run at 20:04 EDT 09-23 (= 05:34 IST 09-24) wrote live_predictions/2026-09-23_15d5pct.json over the committed 09-23 basket (commit 0e15a76) with a different 8 names, and render_basket_report re-rendered basket_report_2026-09-23.md and daily_actions_2026-09-23.md from it.
correction: Committed files restored from git before anything was committed. as_of_date now = datetime.now(Asia/Kolkata).date(); generator raises SystemExit if the target file is tracked in git. The convergence emission is live_predictions/2026-09-24_15d5pct.json.
lesson: An invariant that exists only in a document is a hope. Put the guard at the write site. And the market's date is IST, not whatever timezone the laptop is in.

claim: NEWS_EVENTS freshness contract (5 bd) green => news_event_features.parquet is current.
what_was_wrong: build_news_event_features.py padded every symbol's date index +30 days past its last event, so the parquet carried 51,066 forward-dated rows (max trade_date 2026-10-23 on 2026-09-23). The file-level max-date check could never fail however stale the event store got.
correction: Rows clipped to trade_date <= today (IST) at write; rebuilt, max now 2026-09-24, gate still green on real data.
lesson: A freshness check reads the max date, so any writer that pads forward blinds it. Future-dated rows are a gate bug, not harmless padding.

claim: run_weekly_pipeline.sh step 3 runs miss_learner on last week's Monday->Friday window.
what_was_wrong: LAST_FRIDAY used (weekday+3)%7+7, which returns the Friday BEFORE LAST_MONDAY on any Mon-Thu run. 09-22 and 09-24 runs logged window 2026-09-14 -> 2026-09-11 with empty counts (logs/miss_learnings.jsonl).
correction: LAST_FRIDAY = LAST_MONDAY + 4 days; miss_learner re-run for 2026-09-14 -> 2026-09-18.
lesson: Derive dependent dates from each other, not from two independent clock formulas.
